igcse-0580-intro-algebra-letters.description: Read what a letter stands for and write simple expressions from everyday quantities.

sections.title: What can a letter represent?
sections.label: Groups
sections.intro: A letter can stand for a quantity that changes. If one bag contains n items, another bag with the same contents also has n items.

blocks.html: Write \(3n\) for three copies of \(n\). The coefficient counts the copies.

figure.alt: Three equal bags followed by three loose counters.
figure.caption: The three bags each stand for \(n\) counters. The loose counters add three more.

blocks.prompt: There are 2 bags with \(n\) counters in each bag, plus 11 loose counters. Write an expression for the total.
blocks.solution:
Multiply the number of bags, 2, by the number of counters in each bag, \(n\).

The loose counters add \(11\) to the product.

The expression is \(2n+11\).

retry.feedback: The number of bags and the number inside each bag need multiplying.

blocks.html: An expression gives a rule that works for different values of the letter.

blocks.prompt: There are 5 bags with \(n\) counters in each bag, plus 14 loose counters. Write an expression for the total.
blocks.solution:
Multiply the number of bags, 5, by the number of counters in each bag, \(n\).

The loose counters add \(14\) to the product.

The expression is \(5n+14\).

retry.feedback: The number of bags and the number inside each bag need multiplying.

sections.title: Where do I start with a difference?
sections.label: Order
sections.intro: Start from the quantity named after 'less than'. Then take away the stated amount.

blocks.prompt: Write an expression for 12 less than a number \(x\).
blocks.hint: The words describe a change starting from the named number.
blocks.solution:
Start from the named number. 'Less than' tells you how much to take away.

Subtract \(12\) from \(x\).

The expression is \(x-12\).

retry.feedback: Subtracting x from the given amount goes in the opposite order.

blocks.html: Read the words back from your expression to check the order.

blocks.prompt: Write an expression for 15 less than a number \(x\).
blocks.hint: The words describe a change starting from the named number.
blocks.solution:
Start from the named number. 'Less than' tells you how much to take away.

Subtract \(15\) from \(x\).

The expression is \(x-15\).

retry.feedback: Subtracting x from the given amount goes in the opposite order.

sections.title: When does a group need brackets?
sections.label: Brackets
sections.intro: Work out what belongs to one group first. When there are several copies, the multiplication must apply to the whole group.

blocks.prompt: A print shop makes 7 packs. Each pack contains \(a\) large cards and 6 small cards. Write an expression for the total number of cards.
blocks.hint: The number of packs multiplies the complete contents of one pack.
blocks.solution:
One complete pack contains both sizes of card. Add the part that varies to the fixed number.

Multiply one full pack, \(a+6\), by \(7\). Use brackets to keep the two sizes together.

The expression is \(7(a+6)\).

retry.feedback: This counts the small cards only once. Each pack has both kinds.

blocks.html: Keeping brackets links the fixed and changing parts of the same group.

blocks.prompt: A print shop makes 10 packs. Each pack contains \(a\) large cards and 3 small cards. Write an expression for the total number of cards.
blocks.hint: The number of packs multiplies the complete contents of one pack.
blocks.solution:
One complete pack contains both sizes of card. Add the part that varies to the fixed number.

Multiply one full pack, \(a+3\), by \(10\). Use brackets to keep the two sizes together.

The expression is \(10(a+3)\).

retry.feedback: This counts the small cards only once. Each pack has both kinds.

revision.body:
What can a letter represent?

Write \(3n\) for three copies of \(n\). The coefficient counts the copies.

Where do I start with a difference?

Seven less than \(x\) is \(x-7\).

When does a group need brackets?

For four copies of \(a+3\), write \(4(a+3)\).
revision.checks:
1. There are 6 bags with \(n\) counters in each bag, plus 7 loose counters. Write an expression for the total.

    Answer. \(x-8\)
revision.examTip: Keeping brackets links the fixed and changing parts of the same group.

igcse-0580-intro-algebra-substitution.description: Replace one letter with a given value, including negatives and fractions.

sections.title: What does substituting a value mean?
sections.label: One
sections.intro: Replace the letter everywhere it appears. Keep the operations in the rule unchanged.

figure.alt: Two boxes for the two successive steps in a number rule.
figure.caption: With input \(7\), double it first and then add five.

blocks.hint: Use multiplication where the number is next to the letter.
blocks.solution:
Replace \(x\) with \(2\) to get \(12\times 2+14\).

Multiply first, then add \(14\).

The answer is \(38\).

retry.feedback: The coefficient multiplies the substituted value.

blocks.hint: Use multiplication where the number is next to the letter.
blocks.solution:
Replace \(x\) with \(5\) to get \(15\times 5+6\).

Multiply first, then add \(6\).

The answer is \(81\).

retry.feedback: The coefficient multiplies the substituted value.

sections.title: What changes when the number is negative?
sections.label: Negative
sections.intro: Write brackets around the value before raising it to a power or subtracting it.

blocks.html: The base in \((-4)^2\) is the whole number \(-4\).

blocks.hint: Square the whole negative value inside brackets.
blocks.solution:
Put the entire negative value in brackets: \((-11)^2-14\).

The square is \(121\) because both factors are negative. Subtract \(14\) after squaring.

The answer is \(107\).

retry.feedback: The square of a negative number is positive. Put the substituted value in brackets.

blocks.html: The negative sign is part of the value you substitute.

blocks.hint: Square the whole negative value inside brackets.
blocks.solution:
Put the entire negative value in brackets: \((-2)^2-7\).

The square is \(4\) because both factors are negative. Subtract \(7\) after squaring.

The answer is \(-3\).

retry.feedback: The square of a negative number is positive. Put the substituted value in brackets.

sections.title: How do I substitute a fraction?
sections.label: Fractions
sections.intro: Put the fraction where the letter was. Read the operations outside the fraction afterwards.

blocks.html: Multiply or divide before adding or subtracting unless brackets change the order.

blocks.hint: Multiply the fraction by the coefficient before adding the constant.
blocks.solution:
Replace \(p\) by \(\frac{1}{6}\). Multiply it by \(6\).

Then add \(3\) to the product \(1\).

The answer is \(4\).

blocks.html: A coefficient multiplies the entire substituted fraction.

blocks.hint: Multiply the fraction by the coefficient before adding the constant.
blocks.solution:
Replace \(p\) by \(\frac{1}{3}\). Multiply it by \(9\).

Then add \(6\) to the product \(3\).

The answer is \(9\).

revision.body:
What does substituting a value mean?

If \(x=7\), then \(2x+5\) becomes \(2\times7+5\).

What changes when the number is negative?

The base in \((-4)^2\) is the whole number \(-4\).

How do I substitute a fraction?

Multiply or divide before adding or subtracting unless brackets change the order.

igcse-0580-intro-algebra-formulae.description: Match each value to its letter, follow the order of operations and include the requested unit.

sections.title: Which number belongs in which place?
sections.label: Match
sections.intro: Read the given values with their letters. Mark each letter before filling in its value.

blocks.html: Substitute the given number for each occurrence of the matching letter.

figure.alt: Two labelled input cards with separate arrows to the two slots.
figure.caption: Put the value of \(a\) wherever you see \(a\), and the value of \(b\) wherever you see \(b\).

blocks.hint: Keep each value with its named letter. Put a negative value in brackets.
blocks.solution:
Replace both letters: \(5\times3-(-12)\).

The product is \(15\). Subtracting the negative value is addition.

The answer is \(27\).

retry.feedback: Subtracting the negative b makes the total go up.

blocks.html: Two different letters can represent different values.

blocks.hint: Keep each value with its named letter. Put a negative value in brackets.
blocks.solution:
Replace both letters: \(8\times6-(-4)\).

The product is \(48\). Subtracting the negative value is addition.

The answer is \(52\).

retry.feedback: Subtracting the negative b makes the total go up.

sections.title: Which value changes and which stays fixed?
sections.label: Context
sections.intro: Read the sentence that defines each letter. For a cost rule, a fixed fee can appear as a separate term.

blocks.html: Only multiply the part of the formula that contains the variable being replaced.

blocks.prompt: A workshop charges \(C=5+11n\) pounds for \(n\) tickets. Find the total cost when the group buys 5 tickets.
blocks.hint: The fixed charge is paid once. Multiply only the charge per ticket.
blocks.solution:
Put \(5\) in place of \(n\). The fixed amount \(5\) stays the same.

The ticket cost is \(11\times5=55\). Add the fixed charge.

The answer is \(60\).

retry.feedback: The workshop adds the fixed charge once for the group.

blocks.html: A fixed part of the rule is counted once.

blocks.prompt: A workshop charges \(C=8+3n\) pounds for \(n\) tickets. Find the total cost when the group buys 8 tickets.
blocks.hint: The fixed charge is paid once. Multiply only the charge per ticket.
blocks.solution:
Put \(8\) in place of \(n\). The fixed amount \(8\) stays the same.

The ticket cost is \(3\times8=24\). Add the fixed charge.

The answer is \(32\).

retry.feedback: The workshop adds the fixed charge once for the group.

sections.title: What happens above and below the fraction bar?
sections.label: Fraction
sections.intro: The fraction bar separates two groups. Work out the value of each group before dividing.

blocks.html: Preserve brackets and fraction bars when replacing values.

blocks.prompt: Each tray has mass \(w\) kg. Use \(w=\frac{M-b}{n}\), where \(M\) is the combined mass of the trays and their crate, \(b\) is the crate mass and \(n\) is the number of identical trays. Find \(w\) when \(M=52\), \(b=9\) and \(n=5\). Give an exact value in kilograms.
blocks.hint: Finish the full numerator before dividing by the number of trays.
blocks.solution:
Put the combined mass and crate mass above the division bar, and the count below it.

The tray mass without its crate is \(52-9=43\). Then divide by \(5\).

The answer is \(\frac{43}{5}\).

blocks.html: Dividing one part of the numerator separately changes the formula.

blocks.prompt: Each tray has mass \(w\) kg. Use \(w=\frac{M-b}{n}\), where \(M\) is the combined mass of the trays and their crate, \(b\) is the crate mass and \(n\) is the number of identical trays. Find \(w\) when \(M=61\), \(b=8\) and \(n=8\). Give an exact value in kilograms.
blocks.hint: Finish the full numerator before dividing by the number of trays.
blocks.solution:

The tray mass without its crate is \(61-8=53\). Then divide by \(8\).

The answer is \(\frac{53}{8}\).
